subject: Re: Private deployment - BYOK, escrow release conditions and operator telemetry
messages:
From: Emma Tran <emma.tran@greenbridgehealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Mark Hobbs <mark.hobbs@greenbridgehealth.com>, security@greenbridgehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment questions - operator telemetry, BYOK escrow conditions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Before we move forward with the Private deployment procurement, our security and legal teams asked for clarity on a few items that will determine whether we go BYOK (customer-managed keys) or accept Redwood-managed keystores. High level items: 

1) Operator telemetry: we need a short bulleted matrix that lists what telemetry is collected by Redwood operators on-prem/VPC (auth events, process-level logs, model cache metadata, token-level content/logs). We need retention windows and which of those are accessible to Redwood support/ops.

2) BYOK escrow release conditions: GreenBridge requires a clear, contractually-enforceable escrow release process for CMK recovery if Redwood ceases operations or in the event of insolvency. Please outline escrow custodian, release triggers, and any verification steps.

3) Subprocessors: we need the current list of subprocessors that may be involved in on-prem support (remote diagnostics, patching). If any vendor has access to cryptographic materials in any step, call that out.

4) Cross-border data movement: confirm whether any operator telemetry or debug bundles could leave the US under default support flows. If so, we need SCCs or equivalent controls.

Can you send a concise response and any doc attachments? Emma (legal) and Mark (procurement) are on c.c.

Thanks,
Emma Tran
VP Legal & Compliance
GreenBridge Health

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Emma Tran <emma.tran@greenbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Mark Hobbs <mark.hobbs@greenbridgehealth.com>, security@greenbridgehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions - operator telemetry, BYOK escrow conditions

Hi Emma — thanks for laying these out. Below is a concise summary; attaching an initial redline of our standard DPA and a short telemetry matrix for Private deployments. Happy to walk through live.

1) Operator telemetry (summary):
- Auth & audit events: account logins, service account actions, and operator session starts/stops — retention default 90 days; accessible to Redwood SREs for support via role-based tickets.
- Process & system metrics: CPU, memory, GPU telemetry, process crash dumps (no customer payload content) — retention 30 days; accessible to SREs.
- Model cache metadata: cache hit/miss counters and model version identifiers (not prompt or response content) — retention 180 days; accessible to SREs for performance tuning.
- Debug bundles (optional & on-request): may include redacted logs and config dumps; customer control: can be configured to exclude any artifacts that might contain secrets/content. Default flow: redacted by customer-provided script or captured locally and transferred only with explicit customer approval.

2) BYOK escrow release conditions (short):
- Escrow custodian: we use a neutral third-party escrow agent (named in the contract); Redwood will add the custodian name in the DPA annex.
- Release triggers: (a) Redwood insolvency/cease of operations, (b) mutually agreed termination with unresolved key return, (c) court order.
- Verification steps: escrow agent requires notarized request, copy of signed termination notice, and a 30-day cure period (unless court-ordered). Keys are delivered to the customer’s registered KMS owner and logged.
- Cryptographic handling: keys are transferred in an encrypted envelope; we can support HSM key export formats or wrapped key material depending on customer KMS.

3) Subprocessors (high level):
- Remote diagnostics partner: OpsAssist (support-only access to anonymized system metrics; no private key access by default).
- Patch management vendor: InfraWorks (can perform patching under customer-approved runbooks; cryptographic materials are not accessed).
- On-prem field engineers (3rd-party): only involved under supervised break-glass with customer approval and under explicit contract language.

4) Cross-border movement:
- Default support flows keep debug bundles and telemetry within the deployment region unless the customer permits transfer to Redwood support engineers. We are prepared to add SCCs and contractual prohibitions on transfers outside the US for GreenBridge.

Attachments: telemetry-matrix.pdf and initial DPA redline.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to provide an escrow annex draft and name of escrow agent by Friday 6/18.
- Customer to confirm whether debug bundles may be transferred to Redwood support for the first 90 days of onboarding.

If helpful, I can loop in Irene (privacy/legal) and Marissa (solutions/ops) to confirm the escrow wording and subprocessor access controls.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy & Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment questions - GreenBridge - action items

Team — forwarding GreenBridge's questions and my draft answers (below). High priority: finalize escrow annex language and confirm whether OpsAssist or InfraWorks require any change to default contracts for BYOK customers. Quick asks: 

- Irene: please review the proposed release triggers and the 30-day cure period. Legal wants the notarized + termination notice flow but GBH may push for a shorter cure window. Recommend alternative language if necessary.
- Marissa: check operational feasibility of the customer-controlled redaction script for debug bundles. Can we operationalize that for onboarding? Any constraints on support windows?
- Karthik: confirm that patching/remediation runbooks can be written such that no wrapped key material is uploaded to vendor consoles. If not, we need a procurement exception or change in vendor responsibilities.

I plan to send GreenBridge an escrow-agent name and a more detailed subprocessor table by Friday 6/18. Please reply inline.

—Sofia

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Tran <emma.tran@greenbridgehealth.com>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-17T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions - operator telemetry, BYOK escrow conditions

Hi Emma and team — thanks for the patience. A few clarifications and commitments from Redwood legal/privacy: 

1) Escrow annex (commitment): Redwood confirms we will include the escrow agent "Northpoint Escrow Services" in the DPA annex and will add explicit release triggers as Sofia proposed. Legal will offer two options for the cure period: 30 days (standard) or a negotiated 10-day window for critical customers; default remains 30 days unless GreenBridge requests the expedited term.

2) Operator telemetry access & retention (contract commitments):
- We will contractually commit to retention windows in the DPA annex (Auth/audit 90 days; sys metrics 30 days; cache metadata 180 days).
- Access to telemetry by Redwood personnel will be restricted to named roles (SRE, on-call support) and auditable via access logs. We will include a clause that requires customer approval for support engineers to retrieve debug bundles that contain any potentially sensitive payloads.

3) Subprocessor statements:
- We will provide a 30-day advanced notice if any subprocessor that could touch telemetry or support artifacts changes.
- OpsAssist and InfraWorks will be contractually prohibited from accessing cryptographic key material. Any field engineer engagement will require a customer-signed break-glass authorization and on-site supervision or secure remote session with customer-approved session capture disabled.

4) Cross-border transfers:
- Redwood will add SCCs (EU standard clauses) or comparable contractual language on request; for GreenBridge we will prohibit transfer outside the US unless explicitly authorized in writing.

Next steps / deliverables by 2028-06-20:
- Final escrow annex draft (Irene) — will attach to DPA redline.
- Detailed subprocessor table with access scope (Marissa).
- Tech playbook snippet for redaction script and debug bundle procedures (Marissa + Karthik).

Emma/Mark — if these commitments align, I will push the updated redline into the shared Drive and ask procurement to route the DPA for signature.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
